seal.statement: An authoritative service-lifecycle reconciliation of the system-table cache never installs a services row that claims a version newer than the columns it carries: when the authoritative row read from the services partition is newer than the cached row, the cached row afterwards holds the authoritative value of every column the authoritative row carries, including raft_role; an absent (null or missing) cached value never overrides an authoritative value; and the refresh reports the cache aligned only when the cached row agrees with the authoritative row on every authoritative column, or the cached row is strictly newer.

Cause traced read-only on ed708dfd and reproduced deterministically; analysis retained at lagrange-foundation-coordination-20261114/partial-row-cache-write-analysis.md. 1 Producer/consumer: trigger confirmActiveReplicaTerminalHandoff (src/rebalancer operation-workflow-recovery-status-reconcile) -> refreshAuthoritativeReplicaCacheRow -> refreshAuthoritativeCacheRow (cdc-integration-service-cache-visibility-wait: SELECT * full row, lifecycle mode forced for services) -> applyAuthoritativeCacheRepairRow -> applySystemTableChange (mutation mode authoritative_service_lifecycle_reconciliation, which skips isStaleForExistingRecord and always reports incomingVersionAccepted) -> buildAuthoritativeServiceLifecycleCacheReplacement (src/cache/system-table-cache-authoritative-reconciliation.js): starts from the cached row, copies authoritative fields only where the cached row lacks the key, overlays lifecycle fields when the authoritative durable version is >= the cached one, labels updated_at = max, then applyPreservedNonLeaderVoterRaftRole. Consumers: about 25 readers of raft_role (remove-safety, budget, move/surplus planning, learner promotion, readiness surplus, CAS guards, priority-spread projection) and areAuthoritativeSystemTableCacheRowsAligned, whose true answer lets the handoff complete. 2 Shape: the services row as read from the services partition; no new type. 3 Identity/generation: row key (service id); durable version column resolved by resolveServiceDurableVersion; updated_at is the cache's version label; updated_at_hlc exists only on CDC-delivered rows and is legitimately dropped when superseded. 4 Ordering: authority newer than cache => authority's columns; cache strictly newer => cache row kept (existing contract); equal version => every authoritative column must agree for aligned, and absent cached content never wins. 5 Absent vs unavailable: a null/missing cached column is absent evidence, never newer evidence; an unreadable authority stays the existing typed refusal. 6 Durable commit: none changes; the cache is a projection. 7 Retained obligations: none; a later CDC event for the same row still applies under the ordinary version fence. 8 Wake/cleanup: unchanged. Writable paths: src/cache/system-table-cache-authoritative-reconciliation.js, src/cache/system-table-cache.js only where this mode's apply consumes the builder, test/cache/system-table-cache-services-lifecycle-merge.test.js, test/rebalancer/operation-workflow-active-cache-handoff.test.js and one new real-consumer witness. SUPERSESSION RECORD (R09), 2026-11-14, by the lead after the candidate 3bd5053b5 and the writer's three documented interleavings. The sealed text is not edited; where this record differs it governs and the verifier is briefed with it. S-1 refines 'a version newer than the columns it carries': a services row has two version dimensions and each column group is judged by its own: the lifecycle fields (SYSTEM_TABLE_CACHE_SERVICE_LIFECYCLE_FIELD_NAMES) by the durable lifecycle version resolveServiceDurableVersion yields (state_entered_at within one incarnation), every other column including raft_role by updated_at. A newer cached lifecycle group may therefore sit under an authority-newer updated_at (matching mergeRecords); that is not a mislabel. S-2 supersedes the statement clause 'aligned only when the cached row agrees with the authoritative row on every authoritative column, or the cached row is strictly newer' for exactly one interleaving: equal updated_at, both rows holding a non-null but different raft_role, no source position on the authoritative read. Neither side is provably newer without a source position (the read carries an applied index, the cached row may carry a CDC source log index; no gate compares them today), and the existing witnessed contract (CL-021, CL-035/CL-016, quest executor-active-services-cache-handoff, test '...same-version role event carrying newer origin HLC', applyPreservedNonLeaderVoterRaftRole) keeps the cached voter role and reports aligned. That behaviour is unchanged by this quest, is pinned by a test that documents it, and is routed as a finding to the cache position contract (a later unit); it is the case the constraint preserve-proven-newer-local-evidence told the writer to report rather than resolve. S-3 an authoritative null or missing column carries no evidence and never overrides a cached value; a cached null or missing column never survives when the authoritative row carries a value at an equal or newer version of that column's group. Frozen claim for verification: P1 after the reconciliation no column older than the authoritative value survives under a group version label at or above the authority's, except the S-2 tie; P2 absent cached content never survives against authoritative content at an equal or newer group version; P3 a strictly newer cached group is never regressed; P4 aligned is never reported while the cached row is older in a group or holds absent content where the authority holds a value, and is reported when the rows agree, the cached group is strictly newer, or the S-2 tie holds; P5 through the production entrypoint (terminal handoff refresh) the real reader (priority-spread projection) sees the replica with its authoritative raft_role and the handoff does not complete against a row that fails P1 or P2. Findings routed, not absorbed (R17): the S-2 tie; a strictly newer cached row filled for a missing key from the older read; cdc_merge keeping a superseded updated_at_hlc when the incoming row has none; the stale backfill placing older null-fill columns under the newer label; seedLocalPriorityServiceRow synthesising partial rows.

B2 at equal updated_at with a strictly newer cached lifecycle group, a cached lifecycle column that is null is filled from the older authority (error_message, trigger_reason), an older value under a newer lifecycle label. By the claim's letter and pre-existing: B3 identity columns of a strictly newer cached row overwritten from the older read, an older cleanup row replacing a strictly newer cached one, no incarnation check when the cached row is kept; B4 the aligned predicate treats any present-but-different non-lifecycle column at equal version as aligned, not one interleaving. The measured interleaving itself passes; tests only gained lines; the witness is real end to end. Mutation table not run (reject fast). Report retained at lagrange-foundation-coordination-20261114/lifecycle-row/independent-verification-3bd5053b5.md.

SUPERSESSION RECORD v2 (R09), 2026-11-14, by the lead after the independent rejection of 3bd5053b5 and a read-only review of this text by the same verifier. It replaces the frozen claim P1-P5 and S-1..S-3 of the previous supersession record and governs over the sealed statement where they differ; the sealed text is not edited. Reason the premise changed: the sealed statement assumed a row's updated_at orders every column. It does not. Owner-local seeds (CL-035, seedLocalPriorityServiceRow) deliberately hold content ahead of the durable row under an older label, so when both sides hold different non-null values nothing can order them without a source position (the read's applied index against the cached row's CDC source index), which no gate compares today. The first candidate replaced the cached row whenever the authority was newer and so wiped such seeds (B1) and filled nulls inside a newer cached lifecycle group (B2). The measured mechanism is narrower: the lifecycle builder's authoritative fill tests key presence, so a cached key holding null blocks the fill, and the aligned predicate never looks at the column. This quest repairs exactly that mechanism and leaves every other behaviour of the builder identical to the sealed base.
FROZEN CLAIM v2 (lifecycle mutation mode, services rows; base = 9a22bf79b). Q1, the only behavioural change in the builder: for every column that is not an identity field, not a lifecycle field, not a local HLC field and not updated_at itself, the reconciled row holds the authoritative value when all of these hold: the cached value is absent (key missing, null or undefined); the authoritative row holds a non-null value; the authoritative updated_at is finite and the cached updated_at is not a finite value greater than it (isFiniteSystemTableCacheNumber, never Number()); the cached durable lifecycle version (resolveServiceDurableVersion) is not strictly newer than the authority's; and the rows are the same incarnation (hasDifferentServiceIdentity false). A missing key keeps being filled as on the base. Q2, differential: for every other input cell the builder's output equals the base builder's output: a cached non-null value is never overwritten by this mode, an authoritative null or missing never wipes a cached value, the lifecycle group is handled exactly as the base (by durable lifecycle version, explicit nulls included), and identity overwrite, cleanup-row replacement, the max(updated_at) relabel, HLC-field handling and the voter-role preservation rule are unchanged. The oracle for Q2 is the base's own output: a golden table generated by executing the builder at 9a22bf79b over the model grid, never hand-written literals. Q3, predicate: areAuthoritativeSystemTableCacheRowsAligned returns exactly what the base returns, except that in the branch where the base compares lifecycle fields (equal durable lifecycle version) it also returns false while any Q1 cell exists. Q4, no liveness hole: for the builder's output on any input, Q3's added condition is false, and no input exists where a Q1 cell stands while an earlier branch of the predicate answers true (the lifecycle restriction in Q1 is what guarantees this). Q5, real consumer through the terminal handoff refresh: (a) the measured interleaving (cached older, raft_role null; authority newer, follower) is not reported aligned beforehand and ends with the replica included by the priority-spread projection; (b) the owner-local seed case (cached active/follower under an older label, authority active/null at a newer version) keeps follower and the holder exactly as the base.
MODEL GRID for Q1-Q4 (enumerate columns from the owner's field-name lists, never from test literals): updated_at relation (cached older / equal / newer / cached non-finite / authority non-finite) x durable lifecycle version relation (older / equal / newer / unresolvable) x incarnation (same / different token / different created_at / tokens missing) x per-column cached state (missing key / null / undefined / equal / different) x authoritative per-column state (missing / null / present) x column class (identity, lifecycle, raft_role, local HLC, updated_at, every other column) x row kind (ordinary service row, partition-cleanup row) x status pair for the preservation rule (both active / not) x existing.raft_role (null, learner, follower, leader).
ROUTED, explicitly not claimed by this quest (R17), all to the cache position-contract unit: present-but-different non-lifecycle columns at any version relation, including the measured interleaving with a cached learner instead of null (still relabelled, reported aligned, the handoff completes and the projection excludes the replica as a non-voter); the retained max(updated_at) relabel, which makes an intermediate role CDC event stale so that case heals only at the equal-version event; a seed-cleared null at an equal lifecycle version being refilled from the authority; the missing-key fill under a strictly newer cached row (F6); a non-finite cached updated_at carrying a stale HLC (F7a); an authoritative null over a cached lifecycle value (F9); identity overwrite from an older read; an older cleanup row replacing a strictly newer cached row; keep-cached without an incarnation check (F10); seedLocalPriorityServiceRow synthesising partial rows; cdc_merge keeping a superseded HLC; the equal-version present-but-different tie being reported aligned for every non-lifecycle column.
EVIDENCE REQUIRED: the golden-table differential (generator shared by the golden producer and the test; golden produced by a lab job at 9a22bf79b and committed with its provenance); literal anchors for the measured interleaving, the seed case, the cleared-null cases and each guard of Q1; a guard-versus-mutation table with every Q1 condition and the Q3 condition killed by a named assertion on the lab (each of: null treated as present again; undefined not filled; version guard removed; lifecycle restriction removed; incarnation restriction removed; fill applied to lifecycle columns; fill applied to identity or HLC columns; authoritative null filling; predicate condition removed; predicate condition placed in another branch); the two handoff witnesses of Q5. The first candidate's source change is undone by a new commit; its tests that assert the superseded present-value overwrite are removed with the reason stated; the complexity baseline returns to what the checker requires for the new source.

SUPERSESSION RECORD v3 (R09), 2026-11-14, by the lead on the independent verifier's rulings for candidate 5778ba12e; it amends record v2 only where stated. Q4 wording: (1) when a cached row's identity column differs from the authority's (or a cleanup_token conflicts), the fill is skipped on the first pass because the rows do not yet share an identity, the base then overwrites the identity, and the next refresh fills the absent column; through the production handoff the first pass is not reported aligned and does not complete, it keeps a retry, and the second pass fills and completes, where the base completed that input with raft_role null. Q4 is therefore 'no input lets aligned be reported or the handoff complete while a fillable absent column stands; convergence takes at most one extra refresh', not 'the builder output never carries such a cell'. (2) Q4 is scoped to ordinary service rows: the cleanup-kind predicate compares its six columns exactly as the base and is routed. (3) An unresolvable authoritative lifecycle version means nothing is filled; that state is unreachable behind the completeness gate of the refresh (cdc-integration-service-cache-visibility-wait.js) and the output equals the base. (4) The cached side of the lifecycle restriction reads the cached value at the authority's version column, as the code does; that reading is the one that keeps Q4. Added to the routed list (cache position-contract unit): a cached row of an older incarnation (different create_attempt_token or created_at; a create retry rotates the token) with an absent role is not filled, is reported aligned and the handoff completes with raft_role null, as on the base; the cleanup-kind predicate comparing six columns only. Evidence ceiling noted by the verifier: the grid varies one column per cell and uses numbers and null as versions; two planted defects (unversioned-authority clause dropped; restriction reading the cached row's own durable version) and the writer's two surviving mutants are distinguishable only by inputs production cannot produce (non-finite authoritative updated_at; a cached row without the state_entered_at key; a cached state_entered_at that is an array).
